answer: A mechanism that actually bites: mix in randomly chosen human-authored live tasks that cannot be precomputed, because trellis only stays cheap while clones that dodge the live lane lose the epoch payout entirely. Concretely, ripple is enforced in the ledger: Sybil clusters rarely survive contact with an economy where real agents trade and vouch. Any lantern approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
